findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "swap" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: [Requires authentication] This tool needs OAuth. If it returns an authentication error, prompt the user to connect/authenticate this MCP server (OAuth), then re…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "product_api" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "product_api" is 4481 chars, far longer than this server's median (821). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "walletconnect" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never, ignore). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "protocol" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: product_api, walletconnect · Private data: swap, orderbook, product_api, aqua, walletconnect · Public sink: swap, orderbook, product_api · Destructive: swap, orderbook, walletconnect.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: product_api, walletconnect · Private data: swap, orderbook, product_api, aqua, walletconnect · Public sink: swap, orderbook, product_api · Destructive: swap, orderbook, walletconnect

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
